title: Chicken Cacciatore
subtitle: Braised chicken with tomatoes, olives, and capers
excerpt: Chicken pieces braised in a rich tomato sauce with black olives, capers, white wine, and rosemary. A hunter's stew, cacciatore means hunter in Italian, that varies by region but always involves a slow braise.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pollo alla cacciatora, or chicken hunter style, is a broad category of Italian braised chicken dishes cooked with whatever foraged or preserved ingredients were to hand, mushrooms in the north, olives and capers in the south. The southern Italian version with tomatoes, olives, and capers has become the most widely known internationally. The dish was popularised in the United States by Italian immigrants and became a staple of Italian-American home cooking.

content.text: Chicken cacciatore is best made with bone-in chicken pieces, thighs and drumsticks, because they stay moist through the long braise and release gelatin from the bones into the sauce. Skin-on pieces should be browned until the skin is very crisp; it will soften during braising but the browning adds colour and flavour to the sauce. Olives go in at the end to keep their texture.

Season the chicken pieces. Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down for 7 minutes until deeply golden. Flip and brown for 3 more minutes. Remove and set aside.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat. Cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine, scrape the pan, and reduce by half.

Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Return the chicken pieces skin-side up. The sauce should come halfway up the chicken. Simmer, uncovered, for 40 to 45 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the olives and capers and heat through for 5 minutes. Taste for salt. Remove the rosemary. Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread or polenta.
